DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra.summary: Mathlib supplies the commutative-algebra background this roadmap consumes and a little more than the document credits: adic completion with `IsAdicComplete`/`IsHausdorff`, complete-local-ring basics (`AdicCompletion.isLocalRing_of_fg`, `residueField_map_bijective`, `spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq`), the fact that an Artinian local ring is adically complete, a full continuous universal property for (Mv)PowerSeries into complete separated linearly-topologised algebras (`MvPowerSeries.eval₂Hom`, `aeval`, `eval₂_unique`, `comp_eval₂`), Krull dimension and the Krull height theorem, `Module.support`/`Module.supportDim`, associated primes, regular sequences (`RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular`/`IsRegular`), the Rees theorem for depth (`ModuleCat.exists_isRegular_tfae`), projective dimension of a quotient by a regular sequence, `IsRegularLocalRing`, `Module.length`, and the whole HomologicalComplex/Homotopy/DerivedCategory/Ext/SpectralSequence machinery. What is genuinely missing is everything specific to this roadmap: there is no depth invariant, no Cohen–Macaulay or complete-intersection predicate, no Auslander–Buchsbaum formula, no catenary/excellent hypotheses, no completed tensor product of complete local rings, no Noetherianness of a completion, no perfect complexes, Tor-amplitude, minimal resolutions, derived completion or derived Nakayama, no Schlessinger criterion or deformation functors, hulls and obstruction spaces, and nothing at all about patching, ultrapatching or component support. Tau Ceti adds only peripheral pieces (Auslander–Reiten theory, an Ext Euler characteristic, `TauCeti.RingTheory.Length`) and no local-ring deformation theory. Every layer is therefore not built, and the roadmap's own statement of what it must construct is accurate.

targets.target: Homotopy-equivalence and quasi-isomorphism API for bounded complexes of finite projective modules
targets.note: Mathlib's homological algebra covers this for an arbitrary abelian category, so the generic API the layer wants to 'build using Mathlib HomologicalComplex, homotopy and derived categories' is already there; only the specialisation to complete Noetherian local O-algebras is new. Note that `DerivedCategory C` needs `HasDerivedCategory` universe data, which is available for `ModuleCat R` via the small-shifted-hom construction.

targets.target: Definition of perfect complex by local finite-projective resolutions
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'perfect complex'` over both trees returns only `Group.IsPerfect` and prose; neither library defines perfect complexes of modules or the `IsPerfect`/`Perf` subcategory of a derived category.

targets.target: Minimal representatives over local rings and uniqueness up to homotopy (minimal free/projective resolutions)
targets.note: No `minimalFreeResolution` or 'minimal resolution' anywhere in Mathlib or Tau Ceti; Mathlib has `ProjectiveResolution` and its uniqueness up to homotopy, but no minimality over a local ring. Tau Ceti has `TauCeti.IsMinimalProjectivePresentation` (TauCeti/Algebra/Module/AuslanderReiten/Transpose.lean) for Artin algebras only, which is a presentation, not a resolution.

targets.target: Tor-amplitude of a complex
targets.note: No occurrence of 'amplitude' or 'TorAmplitude' in either tree.

targets.target: Duals of perfect complexes and derived tensor products
targets.note: There is a monoidal structure on `HomologicalComplex` and a `Tor` bifunctor obtained by left-deriving the tensor product in an abelian monoidal category, but no derived tensor product as a functor on the derived category, and no duals/`Dualizable` structure for complexes of modules. Missing: the whole −⊗ᴸ− formalism the layer states.

targets.target: Derived completion, derived Nakayama, specialization/extension under derived completeness
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'derivedcomplet\|derived Nakayama'` returns nothing in either tree. Mathlib's `Mathlib/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean` is the ordinary module-theoretic Nakayama lemma only.

targets.target: Base-change spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^(j−i)(C⊗ᴸ_A B) and its convergence
targets.note: Mathlib has the abstract notion of a spectral sequence with pages and convergence bookkeeping, but constructs no Grothendieck, hyper-Tor or base-change spectral sequence; `grep -i 'grothendieck spectral\|hypercohomology'` finds nothing. The stated spectral sequence is absent.

targets.target: Derived Mittag–Leffler comparisons and lim¹ for the inverse system of finite coefficient quotients
targets.note: `Functor.IsMittagLeffler` is stated for functors into `Type`, about eventual ranges of a cofiltered system, not about derived inverse limits of modules; Mathlib's `AdicCompletion/Exactness.lean` proves exactness of adic completion for Noetherian rings and finite modules 'directly without using Mittag-Leffler systems'. There is no lim¹ functor (`grep -i 'lim\^1\|lim1\|firstDerivedLim'` is empty), so the retention of a nonvanishing lim¹ has no carrier.

targets.target: Compatible chain-level Hecke actions surviving the inverse system
targets.note: Nothing in either library about Hecke actions on inverse systems of complexes; this is roadmap-specific.

duplicates.note: Also treats Hecke actions on bounded perfect complexes, comparing chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions, and localization over complete coefficient rings — the same chain-versus-cohomology distinction P7's last paragraph insists on, stated there for Hecke algebras.

Owns generic derived completion and complete filtered algebra; P7's derived completion and derived Nakayama for complete local O-algebras are the affine special case, and DD.1 is the atlas's declared owner of the generic construction.
Defines perfect complexes and locally bounded Tor-amplitude conditions (in the v-topos setting), overlapping P7's perfectness/Tor-amplitude targets.
Constructs perfect complexes and their enhancements, and derived pullback on perfect complexes, which is the scheme-level form of P7's perfectness and derived coefficient change.

targets.target: Patching data (R_N,S_N,C_N) with S_N a finite quotient of O[Δ_N], bounded generator rank, uniformly bounded finite-projective presentation
targets.note: No patching construction of any kind in either tree; `grep -rn -i 'patching'` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns only prose about gluing charts and Moebius maps.

targets.target: Ultrapatching with a fixed non-principal ultrafilter; independence of representatives
targets.note: Mathlib has ultrafilters, filter products/germs and model-theoretic ultraproducts (Łoś's theorem), which is the ambient tool, but no ultraproduct of a system of modules or complexes over a tower of rings and no ultrapatching construction.

targets.target: Uniform bounds, compactness of finite-presentation data, cofinality before the limit
targets.note: The compactness/diagonal-subsequence argument for presentation data over a tower has no analogue in either library.

targets.target: S_∞ = O[[z₁,…,z_q]] and the patched base R_∞ with its continuous action on C_∞
targets.note: The ring O[[z₁,…,z_q]] exists in Mathlib as `MvPowerSeries (Fin q) O`, is known Noetherian for finitely many variables and has the continuous universal property; the patched objects R_∞, C_∞ and their compatible actions do not exist.

targets.target: Augmentation isomorphism C_∞⊗ᴸ_{S_∞}O ≅ C_original and comparison of finite-level Hecke actions
targets.note: Depends on the patched objects and on derived tensor products, neither of which is present.

duplicates.note: States the same ultrapatching interface — fixing a non-principal ultrafilter as in ACC+ §6.4.1, boundedness and compatibility hypotheses, identification of the specialization with the original complex, and the Remark 6.4.13 independence caveat — but explicitly assigns the abstract construction to this owner and keeps only the arithmetic verification.
'Apply the abstract patching construction to the actual rings and modules' — the GL₂ instance of P8/R03.5, restating the presentation, depth, framing-variable and support bookkeeping.
Constructs the auxiliary Hecke modules and finite group actions and the required freeness over O[Δ_N], which is the arithmetic input P8 declines to infer from cardinality of a covering.

targets.target: Inequalities relating codimension of support, projective dimension and Tor-amplitude over a regular local base
targets.note: Mathlib has support dimension, projective dimension and their behaviour under regular sequences over a Noetherian local ring, plus Krull's height theorem, but not the codim(Supp) ≤ pd inequality (New Intersection / Auslander–Buchsbaum route) and no Tor-amplitude at all. Note `projectiveDimension` is stated for `ModuleCat.{v} R` with `[Small.{v} R]` and needs `IsNoetherianRing R`, `Module.Finite R M`.

targets.target: Balanced-dimension conclusions of Calegari–Geraghty, including non-Cohen–Macaulay and torsion cases
targets.note: No Cohen–Macaulay predicate exists in either tree (`grep -rn -i 'cohenmacaulay\|Cohen–Macaulay'` is empty over both), so the statement cannot even be phrased at the baseline.

targets.target: One-degree module theorem as a specialization; integral support versus support after inverting p
targets.note: `Module.support` and `Module.stableUnderSpecialization_support` exist for modules, but there is no support of a complex, no comparison of integral support with support after inverting an element, and no concentration theorem.

targets.target: Component-support transport under finite flat coefficient change, removal of framing variables, specialization of local conditions
targets.note: Nothing about framing variables or component support in either library; `grep -i 'nearly faithful'` is empty.

targets.target: Nearly faithful / radical-annihilator / union-of-components conclusions
targets.note: Mathlib has `Module.annihilator` and `Ideal.radical` but no 'nearly faithful' notion and no theorem of this shape.

targets.target: Algebraic derived Ihara-avoidance lemmas comparing support under a change of auxiliary local type
targets.note: Absent; depends on all of the above.

targets.target: Derived length identity of ACC+ §6.3.4: idempotent localization of a derived T-action on a perfect S-complex, dimension-zero vanishing and dimension-one generic-length Euler characteristic after reduction mod f
targets.note: `Module.length` and finite-length theory exist, and Tau Ceti has an Ext Euler characteristic and finite length of a quotient by a nonzerodivisor; the derived action, idempotent localization, excellence hypothesis and the dimension-zero/dimension-one length formula are all absent, and there is no `IsExcellentRing` predicate (`grep -i excellent` is empty in both trees).

duplicates.note: States the same comparison of patched complexes for two systems of local conditions, component support, characteristic-zero localization, near faithfulness and the derived Ihara-avoidance support implication, as the arithmetic verification of P9's algebraic theorems.

Local component matching and the patched-support argument, with the same warning that a patched Cohen–Macaulay module on one component proves nothing on another — the GL₂ instance of P9's component-support conclusions.

Same roadmap: R03.6 states support transport along flat maps, coefficient changes and removal of framing variables, and faithful/nearly-faithful/union-of-components conclusions, at module level; P9 restates them at complex level.

targets.target: The coefficient categories: Artinian local O-algebras with fixed residue field, and complete Noetherian local O-algebras with local continuous morphisms
targets.note: All the ingredient predicates exist separately, but neither library bundles them into the category CNL_O / Art_O with a specified residue-field identification; there is no such category object anywhere (`grep -i 'coefficient categor'` over both trees is empty).

targets.target: Presentation of a complete local ring as the inverse limit of its Artinian quotients
targets.note: Mathlib identifies a complete local ring with lim R/mⁿ (that *is* `AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal R) R`, with `IsAdicComplete` saying the canonical map is bijective), proves the completion of a Noetherian local ring is again local and complete (`AdicCompletion.isLocalRing_of_fg`, `AdicCompletion.isAdicComplete_of_fg`), and has an unnamed instance at Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Noetherian.lean:38 giving `IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal A) A` for A Artinian local, so each R/mⁿ is an adically complete Artinian local quotient. What is missing is the statement packaged as an inverse limit over the cofiltered system of Artinian quotients together with its universal property in the coefficient category.

targets.target: Continuous maps from power-series rings into complete local rings
targets.note: This target is already in the library, more generally than asked: for `S` a complete separated topological R-algebra with `IsLinearTopology S S`, a continuous φ : R →+* S and a family `a : σ → S` satisfying `HasEval a` (each a s topologically nilpotent, a s → 0 cofinitely), `eval₂Hom` is the continuous ring map out of `MvPowerSeries σ R` and `eval₂_unique` gives its uniqueness among continuous maps agreeing on polynomials. A complete Noetherian local O-algebra with its m-adic topology satisfies these hypotheses. Tau Ceti adds `MvPowerSeries.eval₂_mem_pow` and substitution lemmas in TauCeti/RingTheory/MvPowerSeries/.

targets.target: Completed tensor product over O; when it stays Noetherian and local
targets.note: Mathlib proves the completion of a finite module over a Noetherian ring is the base change along the completed ring, and flatness of the completion, but defines no completed tensor product A ⊗̂_O B of complete local rings and does not even prove that the adic completion of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian (no such instance in Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/). So the Noetherian-and-local criterion the layer wants to state has no carrier.

targets.target: Residue-field extension of the coefficient ring
targets.note: Residue fields and functoriality exist, and completion is known not to change the residue field, but the base-change construction O ⤳ O' realising a finite residue-field extension of a complete DVR (unramified base change / Witt-vector functoriality) is not set up as such.

targets.target: Descent and ascent of finite generation along these maps
targets.note: Generic transitivity/descent of module finiteness is in Mathlib; the continuous/complete-local versions (finite generation detected on the residue field, i.e. topological Nakayama for complete local rings) are not stated, though `IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot` plus `Module.Finite` Nakayama gets close.

targets.target: Explicit API for nilpotent ideals, small extensions and square-zero extensions
targets.note: Nilpotency of ideals and the trivial square-zero extension R ⊕ M exist, but there is no notion of a *small extension* of Artinian local rings (surjection with principal kernel killed by the maximal ideal), which is exactly what Schlessinger's criterion in R03.2 needs.

duplicates.note: Defines deformations over Artinian coefficient rings and change of coefficients, and lists DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 as a dependency; it uses rather than duplicates the coefficient category, but restates the Artinian-coefficient setup.
'Completed tensor products and the fibre products actually used' — owns completed tensor products in the adic/Huber setting, overlapping R03.1's completed tensor product over O.

Constructs completed tensor products with their topology and universal property for Huber pairs; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra is listed as one of its consumers, so the two must agree on which construction is the owner.
Works in the same base category of Artinian local W(k)-algebras with residue field k (KM 7D), so it also needs the coefficient category R03.1 constructs.

targets.target: Schlessinger's criterion (H1–H4) for a functor on Artinian local O-algebras
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'schlessinger'` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns nothing; neither library has any representability criterion for functors on Artinian algebras.

targets.target: Framed representability construction (existence of a universal framed deformation ring)
targets.note: Absent; no deformation functors exist (`grep -rn -i 'deformation'` finds only unrelated uses: deformation retracts in Tau Ceti's homology files and a docstring in Mathlib's FontaineTheta).

targets.target: Tangent-space finiteness of a deformation functor
targets.note: Mathlib has the cotangent space m/m² of a local ring as a residue-field vector space and its finite-dimensionality for Noetherian local rings, which is the ring-side counterpart; the functor-side tangent space F(k[ε]) and its finiteness are absent.

targets.target: Fibre products of Artinian local rings and the exactness conditions on F(A×_C B) → F(A)×_{F(C)}F(B)
targets.note: Fibre products of commutative rings exist as limits in `CommRingCat`, but nothing says a fibre product of Artinian local O-algebras is again one, and the Schlessinger surjectivity/bijectivity conditions on the induced map of functors are not stated.

targets.target: Hulls versus prorepresenting objects, and uniqueness of the hull
targets.note: `grep -i 'prorepresent\|versal\|\bhull\b'` returns no relevant hit in either tree (only 'universal', 'reversal', 'transversal').

targets.target: Relating presentation relations to obstruction spaces
targets.note: No obstruction theory in either library; the only occurrences of 'obstruction' are in prose.

duplicates.note: Proves existence of universal framed rings and of unframed rings under absolute residual irreducibility, and compares framed with unframed by formally smooth power-series maps — the arithmetic instance of R03.2's framed/unframed representability, depending on it explicitly.

Establishes the lower bound on global dimension and the bound on the number of relations over a completed tensor product (KW II Prop. 4.5, Cor. 4.7), i.e. the presentation-relations-to-obstruction-space link of R03.2 in the Galois setting.
Constructs unrestricted local deformation rings, which requires the same representability machinery R03.2 owns.

targets.target: Regular sequences
targets.note: Fully developed in Mathlib for a module over a commutative ring, with permutation, localisation and quotient lemmas; the file is sorry-free.

targets.target: Depth of a module along an ideal, as an invariant
targets.note: Mathlib proves the Rees theorem — for Noetherian R, I an ideal, M finite nontrivial with IM ≠ M, the existence of an M-regular sequence of length n in I is equivalent to vanishing of Ext^i(R/I,M) for i<n — sorry-free. But there is no `Module.depth` invariant: `grep -rn -i depth` over Mathlib/RingTheory finds only Rees.lean and the TODO in RegularSequence.lean ('TODO: … depth'). Missing: depth as a number and all its formulas.

targets.target: Cohen–Macaulay rings and modules
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'cohenmacaulay\|Cohen-Macaulay\|Cohen–Macaulay'` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns zero hits. Nothing to build on beyond the depth and dimension pieces separately.

targets.target: Projective dimension of a finite module
targets.note: Projective dimension exists in the categorical form with `HasProjectiveDimensionLT/LE`, and pd(M/xM)=pd(M)+1 for an M-regular x in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring is proved (sorry-free). Stated for `ModuleCat.{v} R` with `[Small.{v} R]`.

targets.target: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula pd(M)+depth(M)=depth(R)
targets.note: Absent: `grep -i auslander` finds only Tau Ceti's Auslander–Reiten translate/transpose for Artin algebras (TauCeti/Algebra/Module/AuslanderReiten/), which is unrelated. Without a depth invariant the formula cannot be stated.

targets.target: Complete intersection criteria used in patching
targets.note: `grep -i completeintersection` over declarations.tsv and both trees is empty; there is no `IsCompleteIntersection` predicate.

targets.target: Depth and dimension formulas under the local maps actually used
targets.note: Dimension drops by the length of a regular sequence, and Krull's height theorem with dim R ≤ µ(m) are proved. The dimension formula for a flat local homomorphism (dim B = dim A + dim B/m_A B) is not in Mathlib, and neither is any depth formula.

targets.target: Equidimensionality, associated primes and support lemmas for finite modules
targets.note: Associated primes and support of a module are complete in Mathlib; there is no `IsEquidimensional` predicate (`grep -i equidimensional` finds only prose about vector spaces).

targets.target: Catenarity and excellence as explicit hypotheses
targets.note: Neither `IsCatenary` nor `IsExcellentRing` exists; `grep -i 'catenar'` and `grep -i 'excellent'` return nothing in either tree. The layer's own instruction to 'state hypotheses on catenarity and excellence' therefore has no predicate to cite.

duplicates.note: Needs maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules over a hypersurface R=S/(w); it would consume the same Cohen–Macaulay API R03.3 must build, and is the only other atlas layer that states MCM modules as a target.
Uses relative Cohen–Macaulay curves and Gorenstein fibres, so it too depends on a Cohen–Macaulay predicate that neither library has.

targets.target: Extracting a characteristic-zero point from a finite O-algebra together with a dimension or non-torsion statement
targets.note: Mathlib has complete DVRs and module finiteness but no lemma producing a Q̄_p-point of a finite O-algebra from non-torsion-ness; the specific statement (a finite O-algebra that is not π-power torsion admits an O-algebra map to the integral closure of O in a finite extension of Frac O) is absent. The layer's warning that nonzeroness is insufficient is correct and unaddressed by anything in the libraries.

targets.target: Finite-over-a-subring criteria of KW II §10 and their completed versions
targets.note: Generic finiteness/integrality transfer is available, but the specific criteria (a complete local O-algebra topologically generated by finitely many elements is finite over a power-series subring, in the completed setting) are not present.

targets.target: Separating a finite unframed global deformation ring from its framed power-series enlargement
targets.note: Depends on deformation rings, which do not exist in either library.

duplicates.note: 'Arithmetic exports for patching and global lifts' — consumes exactly the characteristic-zero-point and finiteness statements R03.4 owns, in the Galois setting.
Small-prime ordinary completion arguments use the same 'finite over a subring / characteristic-zero point' step of KW II §10.

targets.target: Inverse-limit patching of finite-level rings, modules, presentations and transition data, with the compactness/diagonal-subsequence argument
targets.note: No patching of any kind in either tree. Mathlib has cofiltered inverse limits (`CategoryTheory.CofilteredSystem`, `Functor.IsMittagLeffler`) and compactness of profinite spaces, which are the ambient ingredients, but nothing that patches a system of modules over a tower of rings.

targets.target: Existence and finite generation of the patched module and its power-series action
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Specialisation of the patched module and the depth comparison
targets.note: Absent, and the depth comparison additionally needs a depth invariant that Mathlib does not define (only the Rees theorem in `Mathlib/RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean`).

targets.target: Separating integral assertions from those after inverting π
targets.note: Localization away from an element is standard Mathlib; the distinction the layer insists on is a discipline about statements, not a missing construction, but the statements themselves do not exist.

duplicates.note: Same roadmap: P8 is the complex-level version of exactly this inverse-limit patching (uniform bounds, cofinality, existence of the limit, specialisation), with the derived augmentation replacing the module specialisation.
Applies 'the abstract patching construction' to the actual rings and modules, proving each presentation and depth hypothesis — the arithmetic verification of R03.5.
States the boundedness/compatibility hypotheses the abstract patching theorem consumes, for the arithmetic tower.

targets.target: Support transport along flat maps, coefficient changes, quotient maps and removal of framing variables
targets.note: Mathlib has the support of a module and its behaviour under surjections and isomorphisms, but no base-change formula Supp_B(M⊗_A B) = (Spec B → Spec A)⁻¹ Supp_A(M) for flat or finite maps, and nothing about framing variables.

targets.target: Criteria for a patched module to be faithful, nearly faithful, or supported on a specified union of components
targets.note: Annihilators and minimal primes (the components) exist; 'nearly faithful' is nowhere in either tree, and no theorem of the stated shape exists. The layer's caution that Cohen–Macaulayness does not imply full support is moot at this baseline since Cohen–Macaulayness is undefined.

targets.target: An explicit algebraic theorem for the torsion-free/reduced quotient at which an R=T argument concludes, plus the stronger variant
targets.note: Reducedness and radicals are available as ingredients; the R=T conclusion statements are entirely roadmap-specific and absent.

duplicates.note: Same roadmap: P9 states the complex-level component-support transport, near faithfulness and union-of-components conclusions that R03.6 states for modules.

Compares component support, characteristic-zero localization and near faithfulness for two systems of local conditions, keeping reduced-support equality, equality after inverting p, near faithfulness and integral R=T distinct — the same distinctions R03.6 demands.
States when the generic-fibre or integral R=T statement strengthens, which is the arithmetic form of R03.6's final target.

HabiroCyclotomicCompletions.summary: Neither library contains anything called a Habiro ring: `grep -rn -i habiro` over all of Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns zero hits, so the cyclotomic completion R[q]^S, its expansions, evaluation and Taylor maps, and the connectedness/injectivity theorems are all absent. What is present is a surprisingly complete set of carriers the roadmap does not credit: Mathlib's cyclotomic-polynomial theory (`Polynomial.cyclotomic`, `prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_sub_one`, `cyclotomic.irreducible`, `cyclotomic.isCoprime_rat`, and the crucial evaluations `eval_one_cyclotomic_prime`, `eval_one_cyclotomic_prime_pow`, `eval_one_cyclotomic_not_prime_pow` that are exactly the prime-power adjacency arithmetic HC.4 wants), `IdealFilter`/`WithIdealFilter` giving a linear topology from a directed family of ideals, `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom` for the universal property of a complete separated topological ring, limits in `CommRingCat`, division by monic polynomials with uniqueness (`Polynomial.div_modByMonic_unique`) for the normalized degree-bounded expansion, `Polynomial.taylor` together with `taylor_coeff` and `Polynomial.hasseDeriv` (including `factorial_smul_hasseDeriv`, the factorial-denominator comparison HC.3 insists on), `IsHausdorff`/`IsPrecomplete`/`IsAdicComplete` for separatedness and completeness, and `Ideal.quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient` for the Chinese-remainder decomposition of HC.5. So every layer is genuinely unbuilt as stated, but most of its infrastructure layer — not just ‘Mathlib polynomials’ — already exists, and the cyclotomic arithmetic of HC.4 in particular is much closer to done than the document implies. HC.6 is export and acceptance testing rather than mathematics.

targets.target: The multiplicative monoid generated by Φ_n(q), n∈S, ordered by divisibility, and its directedness
targets.note: `Polynomial.cyclotomic n R` is defined for any ring R (integrally, via `map` from ℤ) and is monic; the submonoid generated by a set and the divisibility preorder are standard. The specific directed monoid and its use as an index set are not constructed anywhere.

targets.target: R[q]^S as the inverse limit of R[q]/(f) over that monoid, with projections and the dense polynomial map
targets.note: Mathlib has all small limits of commutative rings, so the inverse limit exists as a categorical construction, but the ring R[q]^S itself, its projections and the density of the image of R[q] are nowhere defined. No `grep` hit for Habiro in either tree.

targets.target: The topology, completeness and separatedness of R[q]^S, and the universal property for continuous maps to complete separated rings
targets.note: Mathlib's `IdealFilter`/`WithIdealFilter` is exactly the generic device for putting a linear ring topology on R[q] from a filter of ideals generated by the products of cyclotomic polynomials, and `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom` is the universal property of the separated completion for ring homomorphisms into a complete separated topological ring. What is missing is the identification of the S-completion with this completion, together with extensionality by finite quotients.

targets.target: Independence of representatives and non-injectivity caveat for the polynomial map
targets.note: Absent, as is the whole construction. Mathlib's `IsHausdorff` (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Basic.lean:46) is the general shape of the separation condition that would have to hold for injectivity.

targets.target: Cofinality of P_N(q)=∏_{i=1}^N(1−q^i) for S=ℕ_{>0}; identification with lim_N R[q]/(P_N) and with the (q^m−1) system; multiplicity count of cyclotomic factors
targets.note: The key factorisation q^n−1 = ∏_{d∣n} Φ_d(q) is in Mathlib over an arbitrary ring, which is exactly what converts the P_N system into the cyclotomic-monoid system and lets one count multiplicities; the cofinality statement itself is not there. Mathlib has no `Habiro` or `q-Pochhammer`/`(q;q)_n` definition, so P_N(q) has no carrier.

targets.target: Continuous functoriality in R, contravariant restriction in S, identity/composition laws, topological equivalences for cofinal systems, and the tensor-then-complete versus base-change distinction
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib's adic-completion-as-base-change theorem is the closest analogue of the interchange question, and it shows the interchange needs finiteness and Noetherianness — supporting the layer's warning that flatness alone does not license it.

duplicates.note: Lists HC.1 as an input and proves the Habiro cyclotomic expansion for colored Jones polynomials; it uses the completion rather than rebuilding it, but restates the coefficient/truncation conventions.
A readiness checkpoint that aggregates HC.1–HC.3 and HB.6; by its own words 'not a new proof construction', so its targets are literally HC.1's.
Reconstructs a (q^m−1)-complete algebra from a diagram of cyclotomic completions, so it depends on and partly restates HC.1's comparison between the Φ-system and the (q^m−1) system.

targets.target: Successive representatives mod P_N and convergent factorial expansion ∑ a_N(q)P_N(q)
targets.note: Absent; requires the completion of HC.1. Nothing in either tree defines P_N(q)=∏(1−q^i) or a factorial expansion of this kind.

targets.target: Normalized degree-bounded expansion by division with monic polynomials; existence and uniqueness of the normalization
targets.note: Division with remainder by a monic polynomial over an arbitrary commutative ring, with the degree bound and uniqueness of the quotient/remainder pair, is complete in Mathlib — that is precisely the tool that makes the normalized expansion unique. Since each P_N and each product of cyclotomic polynomials is monic (`Polynomial.cyclotomic.monic`), the existence/uniqueness statement of this target is one induction away from library results, but is not itself present.

targets.target: Addition, multiplication and coefficient-extraction algorithms on normalized expansions with congruence correctness theorems and finite-precision dependence
targets.note: Absent; no computational Habiro-ring representation exists.

targets.target: Invertibility of q in the full Habiro ring, its inverse at finite precision, and comparison of polynomial with Laurent-polynomial constructions
targets.note: Laurent polynomials and unit criteria in polynomial rings exist as background; the statement that q is a unit in the completion (because q^N≡1 modulo a suitable product of cyclotomic factors) and its finite-precision inverse are absent.

duplicates.note: Explicitly aggregates HC.2 among its checkpoints; no independent targets.
Its acceptance tests include finite-precision Taylor comparisons over the cyclotomic completion, reusing HC.2's expansion algorithms.

targets.target: Evaluation at a root ζ of order d∈S into R[ζ], through a finite quotient, independent of the truncation
targets.note: R[q]/(Φ_d(q)) is `AdjoinRoot (cyclotomic d R)` in Mathlib's language, and over ℤ the cyclotomic polynomial is the minimal polynomial of a primitive root, so the target quotient exists; the evaluation map out of the completion and its independence of truncation do not.

targets.target: The Taylor map into R[ζ][[q−ζ]] from compatible quotient maps, with constant term the evaluation
targets.note: `Polynomial.taylor r : R[X] → R[X]` with `taylor_coeff_zero : (taylor r f).coeff 0 = f.eval r` is the polynomial-level statement of this target, over an arbitrary commutative ring; the extension to the completion and the landing in R[ζ][[q−ζ]] are absent.

targets.target: Identification of the higher Taylor coefficients with Hasse derivatives, retaining factorial denominators
targets.note: At polynomial level this target is fully built and sorry-free: `taylor_coeff : (taylor r f).coeff n = (hasseDeriv n f).eval r`, and `factorial_smul_hasseDeriv : n ! • hasseDeriv n = derivative^[n]` is exactly the factorial-denominator comparison the layer demands. Only the transport to the completed ring is new.

targets.target: Naturality under coefficient change, root conjugation, order restriction and q↦q^a
targets.note: Coefficient-change naturality of cyclotomic polynomials and of the Hasse derivative is in Mathlib, and `Cyclotomic/Expand.lean` handles q↦q^a at polynomial level (`expand`), which is the raw form of the order-change map. The completed versions are absent.

targets.target: p-adic re-expansion maps and their cocycle law, with topological nilpotence in a proved complete coefficient ring
targets.note: Mathlib's power-series substitution API is built on exactly the hypothesis the layer insists on — `HasEval` requires each substituted element to be topologically nilpotent and to tend to zero — so the general principle 'substitution needs topological nilpotence in a complete ring' is already a theorem-level constraint in the library. The specific p-adic re-expansions ζ_{pm}−ζ_m and their cocycle law are absent.

duplicates.note: Proves that substitution by ζ_{pm}−ζ_m exists in the required completion and constructs the Frobenius-twisted Taylor-gluing condition — the same re-expansion maps HC.3's last paragraph owns, in the number-field case.
Carries 'the actual Frobenius-glued Taylor maps' and the q−1 completion comparison, consuming HC.3's Taylor maps.
Uses Taylor expansion at q=1 to produce the Ohtsuki series, which is HC.3's Taylor map at the order-1 root.

targets.target: Adjacency of cyclotomic orders through prime-power ratios, and p-adic separatedness of R
targets.note: The arithmetic that makes adjacency work is already proved in Mathlib and sorry-free: Φ_{p^k}(1)=p and Φ_n(1)=1 whenever n is not a prime power. p-adic separatedness of R is `IsHausdorff (Ideal.span {p}) R`. The adjacency relation itself and its consequences are not defined.

targets.target: Cyclotomic resultant / comaximality lemmas
targets.note: Mathlib has a general resultant with a Sylvester-matrix definition, Tau Ceti adds monic-normalisation lemmas, and `cyclotomic.isCoprime_rat` gives comaximality of distinct Φ_n over ℚ. The integral statement Res(Φ_n,Φ_m) = p or 1 according to whether n/m is a prime power — the actual input to Habiro's adjacency — is not proved.

targets.target: Passage from a connected chain of orders to injective restriction (Habiro Theorem 4.1) with its full chain hypothesis
targets.note: Absent; no Habiro theorem of any number is formalised in either library.

targets.target: Rootwise Taylor injectivity (Habiro Theorem 5.2) with coefficient-domain and separation hypotheses
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: For ℤ and all positive orders, a single Taylor expansion determines the element
targets.note: Absent. This is the theorem downstream roadmaps (ArithmeticQuantumTopology QT.3/QT.4) list as their input.

targets.target: Evaluation uniqueness (Habiro Theorem 6.1) with the precise infinite-set condition, and the non-surjectivity examples of §7.4
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Lists HC.4 as an input and needs its convergence/injectivity in the completion for the unified invariant; uses rather than reproves.
'Derive integrality and determination results using the existing Habiro injectivity theorems' — the same Theorem 5.2/6.1 statements, consumed.

Proves joint conservativity and the right-Kan-extension conditions for the prime-power chain organisation of finite cyclotomic descent, which is the relative-étale analogue of HC.4's connectedness-to-injectivity passage.

targets.target: Compatible completion of M[q] by the same ideals, as a complete module over R[q]^S; functoriality, finite direct sums, continuous scalar action
targets.note: Mathlib develops the adic completion of a module with functoriality and finite-product comparison, which is the template; the completion along a non-adic directed family of ideals generated by cyclotomic products is not available as a module construction, and `IdealFilter` (Mathlib/RingTheory/IdealFilter/) supplies only the ring topology, not a completed-module functor.

targets.target: Hypotheses for exactness of the completion or a derived-limit correction
targets.note: Exactness of adic completion for Noetherian R and finite modules is proved in Mathlib; there is no lim¹/derived-limit functor anywhere, so the 'derived-limit correction' alternative has no carrier.

targets.target: Extension of the connectedness/injectivity theorem using the p-adic separation of M (Habiro §7.3)
targets.note: Absent; depends on HC.4, which is absent.

targets.target: Chinese-remainder decomposition for disconnected collections of cyclotomic factors under comaximality
targets.note: The Chinese Remainder Theorem for pairwise coprime ideals in a commutative ring is in Mathlib, and over ℚ the distinct cyclotomic polynomials are proved coprime — together these give the ℚ example the layer asks for, modulo the completion construction. The decomposition of the completed ring is absent.

targets.target: The R=ℚ and R=ℤ[1/p] examples showing how inversion changes adjacency
targets.note: Absent. Mathlib's `eval_one_cyclotomic_prime` (Φ_{p^k}(1)=p) is the reason inverting p disconnects the p-power orders, but the worked examples are not there.

targets.target: Comparison of restricted-root-order rings with localizations, and failure of naive localization of the completed ring
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Also treats what happens when primes are inverted, keeping the restrictions on root orders and the decomposition phenomena, and warns against inferring integrality of H_R from that of O_F — the number-field form of HC.5's inversion/components discussion.
Constructs Habiro-complete modules with derived detection and the completed tensor product, i.e. the derived upgrade of HC.5's module completion; HC.5 owns the ordinary version.
K₃-indexed Habiro modules, a specific instance of the completed-module theory HC.5 sets up.

targets.target: Export of complete topological rings, quotient projections, evaluation/Taylor maps, p-adic substitutions and completed modules to HabiroNumberFields and HabiroRings HR.2
targets.note: This is an interface/integration task, not a mathematical statement: it re-exports HC.1–HC.5, none of which exists. Nothing in either library to cite.

targets.target: Acceptance examples: ℤ at q=1 and q=−1, a primitive third root, 1−q, the factorial series ∑P_N, q-inversion, and a coefficient ring with an inverted prime
targets.note: The small cyclotomic polynomials Φ₁=q−1, Φ₂=q+1 and Φ₃=q²+q+1 that these tests evaluate at are all computed in Mathlib; the tests themselves are acceptance checks for HC.1–HC.5 rather than new theorems.

targets.target: The map from the classical ℤ-Habiro ring to GSWZ's rational-number-field case
targets.note: Absent; and the roadmap itself assigns the number-field construction to HabiroNumberFields HB.6, so this is a comparison of two objects neither of which exists.

duplicates.note: The parallel acceptance-test-and-executable-boundary layer for HabiroRings, including a Taylor-versus-value test at one root — the same kind of acceptance example, for the relative construction.
'Acceptance tests and Lean boundary' for the cohomology side of the same family; same process character.
A readiness checkpoint that verifies completion and map-level compatibility of HC.1–HC.3 with HB.6, i.e. the same export/integration bookkeeping HC.6 performs.

HabiroRings.summary: Nothing in this roadmap is built. Mathlib explicitly does not know what a Λ-ring is — `Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Dickson.lean:115` says so in a comment — and there are no Adams operations, no δ-rings, no prisms, no q-Witt rings, no derived/E∞ algebra, no spectra and no solid modules, so HR.1–HR.6 have no carriers for their principal objects. What the libraries do supply is genuine and load-bearing: `Algebra.Etale`/`Algebra.FormallyEtale` with the unique square-zero lifting property `Algebra.FormallyEtale.comp_bijective` (the exact mechanism by which the Frobenius lift φ_p on the p-adic completion of an étale algebra is unique), `Module.FaithfullyFlat`, the full p-typical Witt-vector package with Frobenius, Verschiebung, ghost components, Teichmüller lifts and truncated Witt vectors, adic completion with functoriality and exactness, cyclotomic polynomials with `cyclotomic_expand_eq_cyclotomic` and the Φ_d-factorisation of q^m−1, `Étale/Pi.lean` and idempotent descent for the finite-étale-splitting repair HR.5 demands, and equalizers of commutative rings (`CommRingCat.equalizerForkIsLimit`) for the HR.7 placeholder. The roadmap's own diagnosis — that Φ_m need not be irreducible mod ℓ (Φ₅ over 𝔽₁₁) and that the fracture step must be done componentwise — is correct and is not addressed anywhere in the libraries. HR.7 is acceptance testing rather than mathematics.

targets.target: The category of torsion-free Λ-rings with commuting Adams operations ψ^m, Frobenius congruences and composition law
targets.note: Mathlib states its own gap in a comment at Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Dickson.lean:115 — 'Mathlib doesn't currently know what a Lambda ring is' — and `Mathlib/RingTheory/Binomial.lean` only remarks in its docstring that binomial rings are the λ-rings with trivial Adams operations. There is no `LambdaRing`, no `AdamsOperation` and no ψ^m anywhere in either tree.

targets.target: Equivalent descriptions of 'perfectly covered': faithfully flat Λ-map to a perfect Λ-ring, and faithful flatness of every ψ^m
targets.note: Faithful flatness is fully developed in Mathlib, but 'perfect Λ-ring' and the equivalence of the two descriptions cannot be stated without Λ-rings.

targets.target: Examples: ℤ, free Λ-rings, toric polynomial Λ-rings
targets.note: Absent for the same reason.

targets.target: Unique extension of the Frobenius lift φ_p to the p-adic completion of an étale A-algebra R
targets.note: `Algebra.FormallyEtale.comp_bijective` says that for a square-zero ideal I in B the map Hom_R(A,B) → Hom_R(A,B/I) is bijective — precisely the existence-and-uniqueness step that, iterated along B/pⁿ and passed to the limit, produces the unique φ_p on R̂_p. The ‘Λ-ring base with ψ^p’ setting and the actual construction of φ_p are absent.

targets.target: The linearized relative Frobenius (R̂_p ⊗_(A,ψ^p) A)^∧_p → R̂_p is an equivalence, with functoriality, base-change squares and prime-power iterates
targets.note: The only relative-Frobenius-equivalence statement in Mathlib is `WittVector.frobeniusEquiv`, the bijectivity of Frobenius on Witt vectors of a perfect ring of characteristic p — a different statement with different hypotheses. The linearized relative Frobenius for étale algebras over a Λ-base is absent, and there is no completed tensor product to state it with.

targets.target: Morphisms of pairs (A,R) with Λ-compatibility, and naturality of all later maps
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Owns p-derivations, δ-rings, free δ-algebras and Frobenius lifts, and the equivalence of a δ-structure with a Frobenius lift on p-torsion-free rings; HR.1 explicitly imports the generic δ-ring API from it and keeps only the commuting all-prime Λ-structure.
Also constructs δ-rings and perfect prisms and requires comparing every Frobenius lift with the Witt-vector constructions, overlapping HR.1's Frobenius-lift targets.
Owns the global arithmetic gluing over a perfectly covered Λ-ring A following Wagner Appendix A, so it restates HR.1's 'perfectly covered' hypothesis and its local-to-global Frobenius data.

targets.target: Habiro-complete modules over A[q,q⁻¹]: vanishing of derived Hom from the localization inverting every q^m−1
targets.note: The Laurent polynomial ring and localization at a multiplicative set exist; there is no derived completion in Mathlib (`grep -i derivedcomplet` is empty in both trees), so the defining vanishing condition cannot be stated.

targets.target: The left-adjoint completion functor, its idempotence, the limit description by (q^m−1)-completions indexed by divisibility, and the cofinal Habiro-factorial tower
targets.note: Only the ordinary adic completion functor exists; the derived left adjoint, idempotence and the divisibility-indexed limit are absent.

targets.target: Invertibility of q in the completed coefficient ring, kept distinct from adjoining inverses of q^m−1
targets.note: Absent; depends on the construction.

targets.target: Wagner Appendix B: two-term resolution of the localized module (B.1–B.2), completeness detected on homotopy groups, joint conservativity of cyclotomic reductions (B.3), detection of degree bounds and staticity (B.4)
targets.note: Absent. There is no homotopy-group or t-structure staticity language for modules in Mathlib beyond `DerivedCategory.TStructure` (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/TStructure.lean), which is not applied to any completion.

targets.target: All derived-limit corrections rather than replacing a derived inverse limit by an ordinary one
targets.note: Mathlib has no derived inverse limit / lim¹ at all, so the correction terms have no carrier.

targets.target: The completed tensor product and its symmetric monoidal category with the right unit
targets.note: No completed tensor product in either tree; Mathlib's `AdicCompletion/AsTensorProduct.lean` only compares ordinary completion with base change under Noetherian/finiteness hypotheses.

targets.target: The spectral version and the bounded-below solid-tensor comparison of B.8
targets.note: Mathlib has condensed sets/abelian groups but no solid modules and no spectra or E∞-rings, so neither the spectral version nor the solid comparison can be stated.

duplicates.note: Owns generic derived completion and complete filtered algebra; HR.2 imports it and builds only the Habiro-specific counterpart, so the derived-completion half of HR.2's targets belongs there.
Owns the ordinary (underived) completed-module theory over the cyclotomic completion, including the exactness-versus-derived-limit-correction question; HR.2 is its derived upgrade.
Derived adic completion in the sheaf setting, applying DD.1's completed tensor products and completed colimits — the same generic machinery HR.2 specializes.

targets.target: The finite divisor poset of m and the closed cyclotomic subsets Φ_d(q)=0, d∣m
targets.note: The divisor lattice and the factorisation q^m−1 = ∏_{d∣m}Φ_d(q) over an arbitrary ring are in Mathlib; the closed subsets and their poset organisation as a descent diagram are not.

targets.target: Localization/completion intersection calculations: empty p-adic intersections for different prime-to-p parts; surviving intersections organized by prime-power chains
targets.note: The arithmetic input — Φ_{p^k}(1)=p, Φ_n(1)=1 for n not a prime power, and Φ_{np}=expand_p Φ_n for p∣n — is proved and sorry-free in Mathlib; these are exactly the facts that make the p-adic intersections empty except along prime-power edges. The intersection calculations themselves are absent.

targets.target: Joint conservativity and right-Kan-extension conditions for the finite-localization descent, specialized to these coefficient categories
targets.note: Right Kan extensions exist abstractly in Mathlib's category theory; the descent argument and its conservativity hypotheses in this setting are absent.

targets.target: Wagner Corollary 2.4: gluing derived Φ_d-complete E∞ A[q]-algebras E_d along prime-edge equivalences into a unique (q^m−1)-complete algebra, with the morphism-level universal property
targets.note: Absent: Mathlib has no E∞-algebras or derived completion, and no coherence formalism in which 'not permission to glue arbitrary pairwise isomorphisms' could be made precise.

duplicates.note: Builds the compatible complexes over each cyclotomic completion and applies 'HR.2–3's arithmetic fracture/descent', so it consumes exactly HR.3's descent diagram; the two must not both own the gluing.
Owns the classical version of the same arithmetic: adjacency of cyclotomic orders through prime-power ratios and the resultant/comaximality lemmas that make the prime-edge diagram work.
Owns the comparison between the Φ-indexed system and the (q^m−1) system by mutual cofinality, which HR.3 re-derives in the derived setting.

targets.target: Degree-zero relative q-Witt rings qW_m(R/A) with functoriality and Frobenius/Verschiebung in Wagner's exact domains
targets.note: Mathlib has the p-typical Witt vectors W(R) and TruncatedWittVector with Frobenius, Verschiebung, `frobenius_verschiebung`, ghost components and Teichmüller lifts — the classical model. There is no big Witt ring and no q-deformation, so qW_m(R/A) is absent; the layer's point that ordinary restriction maps do not extend to q-Witt theory has nothing in the libraries to conflict with.

targets.target: The defining quotient/universal construction of qW_m and the ghost description under torsion hypotheses
targets.note: The classical ghost map and its bijectivity when p is invertible are in Mathlib and are the template for 'ghost description under torsion hypotheses'; the q-Witt analogue is absent.

targets.target: E_d = (R ⊗_(A,ψ^d) A)[q]^∧_(Φ_d(q)) and the prime-edge maps from relative Frobenius
targets.note: Absent: needs ψ^d (no Λ-rings) and completion at Φ_d(q) (no such completion).

targets.target: Wagner Theorem 2.9: H_(R/A,m) is static, is the unique completed étale lift, and H_(R/A,m)/(q^m−1) ≅ qW_m(R/A)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Transitions H_(R/A,m)→H_(R/A,d) for d∣m, composition, and identification of the quotient map with F_(m/d) (Remark 2.10)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.target: Naturality of the quotient theorem and invariance under equivalent étale presentations
targets.note: Mathlib proves étaleness is invariant under algebra equivalence, which is the elementary half of 'invariance under equivalent étale presentations'; the rest is absent.

duplicates.note: Imports degree-zero q-Witt rings from HR.4 and owns only the positive-degree q-de Rham–Witt complex; the two layers state the same operator relations and the same warning that there are no compatible restriction maps, so the boundary between them must be kept exact.
Uses the derived m-truncated q-de Rham–Witt objects qW_m dR^i as graded pieces of its filtration, so it depends on HR.4's qW_m.
Owns ordinary de Rham–Witt complexes including genuine restriction maps; HR.4/HQ.4 must import from it rather than duplicate, and the atlas says so explicitly.

targets.target: H_(R/A)=lim_m H_(R/A,m) with canonical equivalence of the divisor system and a cofinal factorial sequence
targets.note: Limits of commutative rings exist; the objects H_(R/A,m) do not, so the limit has nothing to take.

targets.target: The complete-ring universal property and continuous functorial maps inherited from the relative étale construction
targets.note: The generic universal property of the separated completion of a topological ring is in Mathlib; the specific ring is absent.

targets.target: Base change under the precise flatness/completion hypotheses
targets.note: Mathlib's completion-versus-base-change theorem, with its Noetherian and finiteness hypotheses, is the closest existing statement and confirms the layer's insistence that no unrestricted tensor-product formula is a default; the Habiro base-change theorem itself is absent.

targets.target: The equalizer presentation of Wagner Lemma 2.12 by compatible cyclotomic Taylor series with ψ^m-twisted coefficients, with its two arrows
targets.note: The generic equalizer of two ring maps and its universal property are in Mathlib — this is presumably the 'concrete equalizer-ring universal property on current Mathlib' HR.7 refers to. The two actual arrows (completion/re-expansion and relative Frobenius followed by re-expansion) do not exist.

targets.target: Root-of-unity choices, change-of-choice invariance, convergence of the p-adic substitutions, working with the full cyclotomic coefficient algebra
targets.note: Primitive roots of unity, cyclotomic extensions and the topological-nilpotence condition governing legitimate substitution into power series are all in Mathlib; the change-of-choice invariance for this construction is absent.

targets.target: Componentwise repair of the p.18 line: Φ_m mod ℓ is separable with finite étale quotient algebra but may split; idempotent descent and reassembly
targets.note: Mathlib proves `cyclotomic n R` is squarefree/separable when n is invertible and that a finite product of étale algebras is étale (Etale/Pi.lean), which are the ingredients for the componentwise repair; and it proves irreducibility of Φ_n only over ℤ and ℚ — consistent with the roadmap's observation that irreducibility mod ℓ fails (Φ₅ over 𝔽₁₁). The repair itself is not carried out anywhere.

duplicates.note: Requires the q−1 completion comparison and 'the actual Frobenius-glued Taylor maps', and compares with HR.5 and HB.6's explicit GSWZ ring, restating HR.5's Taylor presentation targets from the cohomology side.
Constructs the Frobenius-twisted Taylor-gluing condition and the compatible root-of-unity coefficient rings explicitly; HR.5 must specialize to it, so the two state overlapping gluing conditions.
Owns the classical cyclotomic Taylor maps and the p-adic re-expansion cocycle law that HR.5's equalizer arrows are built from.

targets.target: Recovery of the classical ℤ-Habiro ring H_ℤ (Wagner Remark 2.14) from the relative construction using HC.1–4
targets.note: Neither side of the comparison exists: `grep -rn -i habiro` over Mathlib and Tau Ceti returns zero hits, and the relative construction of HR.1–HR.5 is absent too.

targets.target: Recovery of the explicit GSWZ ring for R=O_F[1/disc(F)] (Wagner Corollary 2.13) by comparison with HB.6's Frobenius-glued ring
targets.note: The coefficient ring O_F[1/disc(F)] is expressible in Mathlib (`NumberField.RingOfIntegers` localized away from the discriminant), and Mathlib knows O_F[1/disc] is étale over ℤ[1/disc] in the sense of `Algebra.Etale` only via the unramifiedness of primes not dividing the discriminant — the two Habiro rings being compared do not exist.

targets.target: The discriminant-inversion hypothesis for the ring comparison, kept separate from the stronger excluded-prime hypotheses of the later regulator/K₃ modules
targets.note: Mathlib's `NumberField.not_dvd_discr_iff_isUnramifiedIn` — a prime p is unramified in 𝒪 exactly when p does not divide discr K — is the reason discriminant inversion makes O_F[1/Δ] unramified, hence étale, over ℤ[1/Δ]; that is the hypothesis this layer isolates. The layer's own statement, and the separation from the later excluded-prime hypotheses, are absent.

targets.target: No naive R-algebra structure without a separate theorem supplying compatible global Frobenius lifts
targets.note: A discipline statement rather than a construction; absent along with everything it constrains.

duplicates.note: Constructs the number-field Habiro ring and proves it agrees with the usual Habiro completion when F=ℚ, Δ=1; this sub-layer is precisely the comparison of HB.6's ring with HR.5's relative construction, so the two share the target and HB.6 owns the explicit ring.
A readiness checkpoint aggregating HC.1–HC.3 and HB.6 for the same number-field Habiro ring and Taylor gluing.
Same roadmap: the atlas gives this sub-layer the same description text as HR.5, and its own targets are the final paragraph of HR.5.

targets.target: Étale degree-zero identification of q-Hodge/Habiro cohomology with HR.5 (Wagner Corollary 3.13), with multiplication, every cyclotomic specialization, q−1 completion and functoriality in (A,R)
targets.note: Both sides are absent: there is no q-Hodge or Habiro cohomology and no relative Habiro ring in either library.

targets.target: Export of complete modules, derived scalar extension, perfect complexes and invertible-module comparisons to Habiro cohomology
targets.note: Invertible modules and the Picard group of a commutative ring exist in Mathlib (`Module.Invertible`, `CommRing.Pic`), but there are no perfect complexes anywhere (`grep -rn -i 'perfect complex'` over both trees finds only `Group.IsPerfect`) and no derived scalar extension.

targets.target: Import of HB.7's K₃-indexed modules and only the supported scalar-extension/Picard comparisons
targets.note: Neither library has algebraic K-theory above K₀: Mathlib has no `KTheory` directory at this pin, and Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.AbelianK0` is the Grothendieck group of an abelian category. K₃ of a ring, and therefore the K₃-indexed modules this layer imports, are absent.

targets.target: An explicit completion map explaining what information disappears after q−1 completion
targets.note: Absent.

duplicates.note: Owns the existence classes and the comparison with HR.5 and HB.6's explicit GSWZ ring and states that HR.6/HB.7 own the line-module comparison — the two layers divide one theorem, and both mention the K₃-indexed information loss on completion.
Constructs the K₃-indexed Habiro modules that HR.6 imports; HR.6 must not reconstruct them.
Owns the crystalline/A_inf/prismatic comparison atlas, which HR.6 explicitly routes through rather than duplicating.

targets.target: Acceptance tests: A=R=ℤ, a nontrivial finite étale arithmetic R, a toric Λ-base, localization at a prime and the resulting cyclotomic component behaviour
targets.note: Testing/validation of HR.1–HR.6 rather than new mathematics; none of the objects tested exists in either library.

targets.target: Φ₅ over 𝔽₁₁ as a guard for the finite-étale-versus-field distinction
targets.note: Φ₅ over 𝔽₁₁ is computable in Mathlib as `cyclotomic 5 (ZMod 11)` (the field instance on `ZMod p` for p prime is the unnamed instance at Mathlib/Algebra/Field/ZMod.lean:30), and Mathlib proves squarefreeness/separability of `cyclotomic n R` but irreducibility only over ℤ and ℚ — consistent with the splitting this test is designed to catch. The test itself is not written.

targets.target: Two elements with the same value at one root but unequal full Taylor expansions there
targets.note: Absent; this is HC.4's value-versus-Taylor distinction, tested here.

targets.target: A concrete equalizer-ring universal property on current Mathlib (Suggested.lean), to be instantiated later by the canonical/Frobenius Taylor maps
targets.note: The generic target of this item is already in Mathlib: `RingHom.eqLocus` is the equalizer subring of two ring maps and `CommRingCat.equalizerForkIsLimit` proves the corresponding fork is a limit, so the 'concrete equalizer-ring universal property' needs no new work. The layer itself notes this is not a Habiro construction.

duplicates.note: The parallel acceptance-and-export layer for the classical completion, with the same value-versus-full-Taylor test and the same process character.
'Acceptance tests and Lean boundary' for the cohomology side of the family.
